Lauren Warhol Caldwell, born Lauren Caldwell, is an American theatre director, actress, and artistic consultant. She served as the artistic director of the Hippodrome Theatre in Gainesville, Florida, from 1993 to 2019. Since 2019, she has worked as an artistic consultant at Black C Art Gallery in Gainesville.
Early life and education
Caldwell was born in Waco, Texas. As a teenager, she developed an interest in theater through community theater productions. She received a Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in directing and design from Baylor University, where she described the training as "almost like boot camp." She earned a Master of Fine Arts (MFA) in acting from the University of Florida.
Career
Early career
After graduating from Baylor University, Caldwell worked in New York City during the 1970s and 1980s as an assistant to actress and singer Liza Minnelli for over a decade, forming a lasting friendship. During this period, she met artist Andy Warhol, who encouraged her to adopt his surname. Following Warhol's death in 1987, she began using "Warhol" as her middle name, noting that more people call her Warhol than Lauren.
Hippodrome Theatre
Caldwell joined the Hippodrome Theatre in Gainesville, Florida, in the late 1980s as an actress while pursuing her master's degree at the University of Florida. Her first performance at the theater was in Eric Bogosian's Talk Radio. After graduating in 1992, she directed the theatre's teen program part-time before becoming full-time director of education in 1993. She became artistic director in 1993 and held the position until 2019. During her tenure, she oversaw more than 100 mainstage productions and directed works including Rupert Holmes' Accomplice (her directorial debut at the Hippodrome), an all-female adaptation of Frankenstein in 2015, The Christians in 2017, Alice in Wonderland in 2006, Gutenberg! The Musical, The Diary of Anne Frank, and George Orwell's 1984. She initiated a partnership with the University of Florida School of Theatre and Dance and established the Hippodrome Acting Company in 2014, a group of approximately 30 professional actors providing a core talent pool for productions. Caldwell aimed to transform the Hippodrome into "another Steppenwolf," known for risk-taking and innovation, favoring provocative shows. Following her departure from full-time employment in 2019, Caldwell remained an acting company member at the Hippodrome and expressed interest in occasional directing.
Black C Art Gallery
Following her departure from the Hippodrome in 2019, Caldwell became an artistic consultant at Black C Art Gallery in Gainesville. She has directed and performed in productions there, including The Stronger in 2020, Journal Entry in 2021, and Jack & Jill II: Alone Together in 2024. In this role, she focuses on writing, promotion, and visioning, embracing "art for art's sake" and aiming to "get risky again."
Other work
Caldwell has served as an adjunct professor and director at the University of Florida School of Theatre + Dance. She directed productions there, including The Importance of Being Earnest. She has also directed staged readings, such as Death of a Driver at Florida Repertory Theatre in Fort Myers, Florida.
Awards
In 2017, Caldwell received the Lifetime Achievement Award in professional theater from the Florida Theatre Conference, recognizing her leadership in developing the Hippodrome as a State Theatre of Florida and her dedication to artists, educators, and audiences.
Legacy
Caldwell's 26-year leadership at the Hippodrome Theatre significantly elevated its status as one of Florida's premier professional regional theatres and a designated State Theatre of Florida. Under her direction, the theatre maintained its professional equity status, produced innovative and provocative works, and contributed substantially to the local economy, with studies citing annual impacts exceeding $4 million from patron spending and operations. Her emphasis on risk-taking programming and community engagement helped build the theatre into a cultural anchor for Gainesville, influencing generations of artists, educators, and audiences. Colleagues have highlighted her nurturing approach to actors and visionary leadership. Actress Sara Morsey praised her for loving and trusting actors, guiding them effectively. Hippodrome co-founder Gregg Jones described her as "a dedicated and visionary artist who has helped build our theater into a local, state and national treasure."
